title: Article 6 — Rights of citizenship of certain persons who have migrated to India from Pakistan

content.overview: Article 6 confers citizenship (at commencement) on certain persons who migrated to India from Pakistan. It distinguishes migrants who came before 19 July 1948 (deemed citizens if domicile conditions met) from those who came on or after that date (citizenship by registration after six months’ residence and prescribed application).
content.glance: Pakistan → India migrants: before 19-7-1948 (domicile rules); on/after 19-7-1948 (registration after 6 months’ residence).
content.study:
Article 6 addresses the Partition migration from Pakistan to India.

Two categories:
1. Migrated before 19 July 1948: treated as a citizen if the person (or either parent or any grandparent) was born in India as defined in the Government of India Act, 1935 (as originally enacted) and the person has been ordinarily resident in the territory of India since the date of migration.
2. Migrated on or after 19 July 1948: may be registered as a citizen by an officer appointed by the Government of India if the person has been resident in the territory of India for at least six months immediately preceding the application and applies in the prescribed form before commencement (or as otherwise provided).

Article 6 is a commencement provision. Continuing regulation of migrants and citizenship is under the Citizenship Act, 1955 (Article 11).

sections.heading: Key structure
sections.body:
Cut-off date: 19 July 1948.
- Before: ordinary-residence + birth of self/parent/grandparent in undivided India (GoI Act 1935 definition).
- On or after: registration route after six months’ residence and application.

sections.heading: Exam checkpoints
sections.body:
1. State the 19 July 1948 cut-off.
2. Distinguish deemed citizenship vs registration.
3. Link to Article 7 (migrants to Pakistan) and Article 11 (Parliament’s power).

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain Article 6.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 6 confers rights of citizenship on certain persons who migrated to India from Pakistan. Persons who migrated before 19 July 1948 and satisfied domicile/birth-in-undivided-India conditions became citizens. Persons who migrated on or after that date could be registered as citizens after six months’ residence and application in the prescribed manner. It is a commencement provision; ongoing rules are under the Citizenship Act, 1955.

examTips: Remember 19 July 1948 cut-off; contrast Art 6 (to India) with Art 7 (to Pakistan).
